classification.difficultyReason: Recognise a scalar multiple and use the common endpoint to establish collinearity.

content.prompt:
$\overrightarrow{AC}=2\underset{\sim}{a}-3\underset{\sim}{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{BC}=8\underset{\sim}{a}-12\underset{\sim}{b}$.

Prove that the points $A$, $B$ and $C$ lie on a straight line.

answer.short: $\overrightarrow{BC}=4\overrightarrow{AC}$. The vectors are parallel and share $C$, so $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BC}&=8\underset{\sim}{a}-12\underset{\sim}{b}\\&=4(2\underset{\sim}{a}-3\underset{\sim}{b})\\&=4\overrightarrow{AC}.\end{aligned}$$
Thus $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ are parallel and share the common point $C$. Therefore $A$, $B$ and $C$ are collinear.
